chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ubayd ibn Muawiya ibn Shurayh, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from Jabir ibn Abdillah al-Ansari, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out intending to visit Fatima (peace be upon her), and I was with him. When he reached the door, he placed his hand on it and knocked, then said: 'Peace be upon you.' Fatima said: 'And upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'May I enter?' She said: 'Enter, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I and the one who is with me?' She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I do not have a headscarf.' He said: 'O Fatima, take the excess of your bedspread and cover your head with it.' So she did.

Then he said: 'Peace be upon you.' Fatima said: 'And upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'May I enter?' She said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I and the one who is with me?' She said: 'And the one who is with you?'

Jabir said: So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered and I entered, and behold, the face of Fatima (peace be upon her) was yellow, like the belly of a locust. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Why do I see your face as yellow?' She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, hunger.' He said (peace be upon him and his family): 'O Allah, Satiator of the hungry and Repeller of loss, satiate Fatima, daughter of Muhammad.' Jabir said: 'By Allah, I looked at the blood flowing from her veins until her face returned to being red. So she did not suffer hunger after that day.'

key_terms.بَطْنُ جَرَادَة: Belly of a locust (idiom for pale/yellowish complexion)

ai.seo_question: What happened when the Prophet visited Fatima and found her hungry?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the intimate domestic life of the Prophet (SAWW) and Fatima (AS), illustrating the Prophet's tender care for his daughter's physical well-being through a specific supplication for sustenance. In Shia tradition, this narrative is often cited to demonstrate the permissibility of the Prophet entering his wife's or daughter's private chambers and underscores the spiritual and physical blessings (barakah) associated with the Ahl al-Bayt. The immediate cessation of hunger after the dua serves as a sign of divine favor and the efficacy of prophetic intercession for the purification of the household.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Ubeyd Bin Muawiya Bin Shurayh, from Sayf Bin Amerya, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from Jabir Bin Abdullah Al-Ansary who said,

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> went out to visit Fatima<sup>asws</sup> and I was with him<sup>saww</sup>. So when he<sup>saww</sup> ended up to the door, he<sup>saww</sup> placed his<sup>saww</sup> hand upon it and knocked it, then said: ‘The greetings be upon you<sup>asws</sup>!’ So Fatima<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the greetings be upon you<sup>saww</sup>, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Can I<sup>saww</sup> enter?’ She<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Enter, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Can I<sup>saww</sup> enter and the one who is with me<sup>saww</sup>?’ So she<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! There is no scarf upon me<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Fatima<sup>asws</sup>! Take the excess of your<sup>asws</sup> bed spread, so cover your<sup>asws</sup> head with it’. So she<sup>asws</sup> did.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The greetings be upon you<sup>asws</sup>!’. So Fatima<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the greetings be upon you<sup>saww</sup>, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Can I<sup>saww</sup> enter?’ She<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> and the one who is with me<sup>saww</sup>?’ She<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the one who is with you<sup>saww</sup>’.

Jabir said, ‘So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> entered and I entered, and the face of Fatima<sup>asws</sup> was pale like the belly of a locust. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What is the matter that I<sup>saww</sup> see your<sup>asws</sup> face as pale?’ She<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, the hunger’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Satiator of the hunger and Repeller of the loss, Satiate Fatima<sup>asws</sup> daughter<sup>asws</sup>  of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>!’ Jabir said, ‘So, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I looked at the blood flowing from its flowing until her<sup>asws</sup> face returned to being red. So she<sup>asws</sup> did not suffer hunger after that day’.
